A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ResCP work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the methods, proofs, tables, and figures can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original forecasting experiments on four datasets, including coverage, interval width, Winkler scores, runtimes, and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments at other coverage levels, synthetic regime-change results, component ablations, and covariate analyses.

M1.justification: The reservoir encoding, similarity weights, residual sampling, interval optimization, temporal decay, calibration window, and ResCQR readout remain unchanged. V2 clarifies implementation and tests component removals without revising the proposed procedures.

E1.justification: V2 adds a synthetic AR(1) dataset with changing coefficients in Appendix D.3, providing a controlled non-stationary scenario. Solar, Beijing, Exchange, and ACEA forecasting coverage is retained; the expanded feature descriptions document existing data.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparators remain SCP, NexCP, SPCI, HopCPT, and CP-QRNN. Identifying CP-QRNN with CORNN clarifies the existing baseline. The new synthetic comparison uses already evaluated SCP and NexCP; component removals are ablations.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands evaluation design with alpha = 0.05 and 0.15 comparisons, calibration curves spanning 70–95% target coverage, and component/covariate controls. The synthetic experiment specifies 10,000 observations and three coefficient changes. Existing benchmark splits, forecasters, metrics, and tuning settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, v2 adds decay/window ablations on real and synthetic data, exogenous-input ablations, calibration diagnostics, and interval adaptation examples. Tables 3 and 7–9 and Figures 2–5 directly examine component usefulness, distribution shifts, and local adaptivity.

E5.justification: Both versions report ± summaries without specifying run counts, seeds, or their statistical interpretation. Additional tables and shaded calibration plots do not document a new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the original sensitivity results remain unchanged, while v2 adds extensive calibration, synthetic, and ablation results. Table 7 reports 89.75% ResCP coverage versus 88.84% for NexCP at a 90% target. Some additions conflict with retained results: the ACEA/RNN ResCQR curve shows roughly 84% coverage at that target, whereas Table 1 implies 72.76%, without reconciliation.

T1.justification: Assumptions 3.1–3.5, Theorem 3.6, Corollary 3.7, and Appendix A proofs remain substantively unchanged. Equation renumbering and explicit Euclidean norm notation do not alter the mathematics; the new AR(1) formula specifies an experimental setting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free ResCP, scalability, asymptotic conditional coverage, and variants for distribution shifts and exogenous inputs.

C2.justification: V2 adds a representation bias–variance explanation and interprets the new ablations as supporting component and covariate choices. Appendix E.2 distinguishes useful Solar covariates from limited Beijing relevance. Appendix E.1 overgeneralizes component benefits across all settings despite exceptions in Table 8.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies the Monte Carlo sample count, the 100-point beta search, Solar and Beijing feature identities, and CP-QRNN's GRU encoder/MLP decoder architecture. These are additional disclosures, not established changes to existing experiments. Hardware and the promised code release upon publication remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lukoševičius's 2012 practical ESN guide and explicitly connects CP-QRNN to CORNN from the already cited Cini et al. work. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Changes include localized explanatory rewrites, renaming Section 3.2, adding an architecture subsection, and organizing new results and ablations into Appendices D–E. Existing sensitivity and implementation sections move to F–G. The main narrative is largely preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds calibration and interval plots in Figures 2–5 and experimental tables numbered 3 and 5–9. Table 3 repeats the RNN subset of Table 8. The original sensitivity figures are retained as Figures 6–10 but moved onto separate end pages, substantially changing the appendix layout.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses missing direct tests of component usefulness and controlled regime changes, while added implementation details improve reproducibility. These provide useful evidence beyond v1's benchmarks and sensitivity analyses. The net gain is limited by overstated component benefits in Appendix E.1 and unexplained calibration inconsistencies: Figures 2–3 show roughly 84% ACEA/RNN ResCQR coverage at a 90% target, versus 72.76% implied by the retained Table 1.
